course.title: AI Agents for Beginners
course.subtitle: From agentic frameworks and design patterns to production, security and computer-use agents.

course.after_note: Continue with the MCP and GenAI petals in this tree, and Microsoft Foundry for the platform layer.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.blurb: What an agent is, the frameworks that build them, and the patterns that make them work.

lessons.title: Intro to AI agents and agent use cases
lessons.objective: What agents are and where they earn their keep.
keys: An agent = LLM + tools + memory + a loop that decides
Workflows are fixed paths; agents choose the path
Good use cases: fuzzy goals, many tools, verifiable results

lessons.title: Exploring AI agentic frameworks
lessons.objective: The framework landscape and what each layer gives you.
keys: Frameworks differ in abstraction height, not in physics
Microsoft Agent Framework / LangChain / autogen: loop, tools, state
Pick the boring one your team can debug at 2am

lessons.title: Understanding AI agentic design patterns
lessons.objective: The recurring patterns of agentic systems.
keys: Reflection: the agent critiques and revises its own output
Tool use: the agent acts on the world, not just talks about it
Planning: decompose the goal before touching a tool

modules.title: The core patterns
modules.blurb: Tool use, retrieval, trust — the three muscles every useful agent has.

lessons.title: Tool use design pattern
lessons.objective: Give the agent hands: functions it can call.
keys: A tool is a described function: name, parameters, purpose — the model reads the manual
Good tool descriptions are prompt engineering for APIs
Fewer, sharper tools beat a junk drawer of fifty

lessons.title: Agentic RAG
lessons.objective: Retrieval when the agent decides what to retrieve.
keys: Classic RAG retrieves once; agentic RAG retrieves until satisfied
The agent can re-query, re-rank, and read tool output before answering
Grounding turns a confident guess into a sourced claim

lessons.title: Building trustworthy AI agents
lessons.objective: Trust and safety in agentic systems.
keys: Trust = correct + safe + auditable — all three, or none
Human-in-the-loop gates where the stakes are high
Log every decision: an unauditable agent is an unshippable agent

modules.title: Scaling up
modules.blurb: Planning, teams of agents, and agents that know what they know.

lessons.title: Planning design pattern
lessons.objective: Agents that decompose goals into steps.
keys: Plan → execute → replan: the plan is a living artifact
Explicit plans are debuggable; vibes are not
Budget the plan: depth and breadth both cost tokens and time

lessons.title: Multi-agent design pattern
keys: One orchestrator, many specialists — conversations, not chaos
Multi-agent adds power AND failure modes; earn the complexity
Pass context deliberately: agents can't read each other's minds

lessons.title: Metacognition design pattern
lessons.objective: Agents that reason about their own reasoning.
keys: Metacognition: the agent knows what it knows, and says so
Self-evaluation beats self-confidence — score before you ship
Uncertainty surfaced early is a feature, not a failure

modules.title: Production and beyond
modules.blurb: Real deployments, protocols, context engineering, memory, and the frontier lessons.

lessons.title: AI agents in production
lessons.objective: What changes when the demo ships.
keys: Production adds: auth, rate limits, observability, cost ceilings
Eval suites are the regression tests of agents
Ship the narrow agent first; widen it with evidence

lessons.title: Using agentic protocols — MCP, A2A and NLWeb
keys: MCP connects agents to tools; A2A connects agents to agents
Protocols turn integrations from N×M into N+M
NLWeb: the web becomes something agents can query

lessons.title: Context engineering for AI agents
keys: Context engineering is prompt engineering grown up: system, tools, memory, retrieved docs — a budget
The context window is finite and priced: curate ruthlessly
What you keep out matters as much as what you put in

lessons.title: Managing agentic memory
keys: Short-term = the window; long-term = your storage design
Summarize-and-store: compress history, keep the facts
Forgetting is a feature — stale memory poisons reasoning

lessons.title: Exploring Microsoft Agent Framework
lessons.objective: The framework in depth, hands on.
keys: Agent Framework: agents, workflows, and observability in one kit
Foundry Agent Service hosts the loop so you host the logic
The code samples in this fork run on it

lessons.title: Building computer-use agents (CUA)
lessons.objective: Agents that drive browsers and desktops.
keys: Computer use: the screen becomes the API — accessibility tree as scaffolding
CUAs fail visually: screenshot everything, replay everything
Sandbox them; an agent with a mouse is an agent with power

lessons.title: Deploying scalable agents
lessons.objective: Scale from one user to many.
keys: Stateless where possible; state in durable storage where not
Queue long tasks; stream progress; never block the UI on a model
Cost scales with users × turns — design the ceiling in

lessons.title: Creating local AI agents
lessons.objective: Agents that run on your own machine.
keys: Local models (Foundry Local, Ollama): privacy, latency, no per-token bill
Local trades capability for sovereignty — pick per workload
The same agent code, a different endpoint

lessons.title: Securing AI agents
lessons.objective: The security chapter — earn it last.
keys: Agent threats: prompt injection, tool abuse, data exfiltration via retrieval
Least privilege for tools; confirm-before-write by default
Security-101's CIA triad applies — with prompts as the new perimeter
